transcript.text: w/m finally died after 12 yrs, whats the best one to buy under £400? family of 5

For a family of five on a £400 budget, I would look at an 8kg or 9kg model from brands like Beko, Hoover, or Indesit. These offer good capacity and reliability for the price, though they may lack some of the premium features found in higher-end models. Since your current machine has lasted 12 years, it is likely reaching the end of its life; if you are considering repair costs versus replacement, a new machine often makes more financial sense at this age. However, before you buy, I want to check if there was a specific fault that caused it to 'die', as some issues (like a blocked filter or a tripped safety switch) can sometimes be fixed cheaply. Did the machine stop working suddenly with no error codes, or did it give any warning signs first?
it stopped mid-cycle 2 days ago with water still in the drum, wont drain, just hums. some lights flashing but no idea which. cheap fix would be good if poss

That humming sound with water still inside is classic for a drainage issue—the machine tries to pump but can't get the water out, so it stops and locks the door as a safety measure. The most common cause on a 12-year-old machine is a blockage in the pump filter at the bottom front. It’s usually free to fix if something like a coin or button has jammed it. Could you switch off and unplug the machine, place a towel down, open that small flap at the bottom, and check what's inside the filter? Let me know if it was clear or blocked.
didn't know there was a filter tbh. will have a go, anything i need to watch for with the water still in the drum?

Yes, be prepared for a small amount of water to spill when you first loosen it—keep that towel handy. Since the drum still has water in it, opening the filter will likely let some drain out, which is normal. Just unscrew it slowly and check if anything like a coin or button is blocking it. Let me know what you find.
ok will unplug it first and have a go. will report back
Take your time with that. Just remember to keep the towel ready for the water spill when you first loosen the filter cap. Once you've checked it, let me know if it was blocked or if it looked clean.
haven't got to it yet, bit busy. will come back once i've looked

No worries at all—take your time. When you do get to it, just let me know if the filter was blocked by something or if it looked clear. If it's clear and the machine still won't drain when plugged back in, we'll look at whether the pump is actually working.
ok will do, just a quick one: model reads WMBF944P on the door rim if you need it. back soon

That model number is helpful for reference. Since you are still busy, just let me know when you have had a chance to check the filter at the bottom front of the machine. If it was blocked and clearing it made the water drain away, that would likely fix the problem immediately. If the filter was clean but the machine still hums without draining once plugged back in, we will need to look at whether the pump itself is working.
still haven't done the filter, will come back once i have. thanks

No problem at all—take your time. Just let me know when you've had a chance to look: if the filter was blocked, clearing it might solve everything; if it was clean, we'll need to check if the pump is actually running.
